title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, not a manuscript note. It is p. 27 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 I (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), with the printed page number 345. It was evidently filed among the manuscript notes on the PD de Rham complex; the neighbouring pages are unrelated computations on automorphisms of the completed PD simplicial algebra A_k*.

The page continues the proof of a proposition in §3 of Exposé IX on how a homomorphism u: G → H of commutative group schemes, flat and locally of finite presentation over S, behaves under specialisation. Here t is a point specialising to s, and K = Ker u. The invariants are the usual ones of a commutative algebraic group over an algebraically closed field: μ (toric rank), α (abelian rank) and the unipotent rank. (3.1.1) and (3.1.2) are semicontinuity relations between these invariants of K at s and at t.

b) Take n prime to the characteristic exponent and to the orders of the component groups (of the quotients of the geometric fibres of K by their reduced neutral components). The number of n-torsion points of such a group is n^{μ+2α} times a contribution from the finite component group. So the counts in (3.1.1) are n raised to the exponents in (3.1.2), by the structure theory of commutative algebraic groups, and b) follows from a).

c) (K_{t̄})^0 is unipotent exactly when μ = α = 0. Since these ranks can only drop under specialisation, unipotence passes from t to s, so c) follows formally from b).

d) Suppose u_t is an isogeny. Then K_t is finite, so by c) (K_{s̄})^0_red is unipotent. Since G_s has unipotent rank 0, K_s is finite. Fibre dimension is constant for flat groups locally of finite presentation (SGA 3 VI_B 4.3), so dim G_s = dim H_s. Hence u_s has image of full dimension (VI_B 1.2), and since H_s is smooth, u_s is flat (VI_A 5.6). The fibrewise flatness criterion at the unit section (VI_B 2.2, 2.5) then gives flatness and quasi-finiteness of u along the unit section over a neighbourhood U of s. The same argument gives u_{s'} flat for every s' in U, so u|G_U is flat and quasi-finite.

e) The first assertion is reduced by base change to the case where S is integral with generic point t. The proof continues on the next printed page.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. There is a typo in the original, 'la premier assertion' for 'la première'.
In c) the typed '(K_{t̄})^o_s' should mean (K_{t̄})^0_red (or ^0), matching the analogous expression in d); the subscript 's' looks like a typing slip.

ideas.what: Counting n-torsion of commutative algebraic groups (n prime to p and to the component-group orders) to read off the toric and abelian ranks μ, α
ideas.modern_name: Torsion counting via Chevalley structure theorem; semicontinuity of toric/abelian rank

ideas.what: An isogeny on the generic fibre spreads to a flat quasi-finite homomorphism near s when G_s has unipotent rank 0 and H is smooth
ideas.modern_name: Extension of isogenies over a base / fibrewise flatness criterion for group schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 IX; uses SGA 3 VI_A/VI_B
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX §3 (proof of 3.1 d)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the published SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (printed page 345), misfiled among the PD de Rham notes. Its content is fully published and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The header and page number match the printed SGA 7 I Exp. IX, p. 345. The '174' at the bottom is the archive folio number.
'(K_{\bar t})^{o}_{s}' in c) likely reads/means (K_{\bar t})^{o}_{red}.
'élévant' should be 'élevant' (typo in the original typescript).
